task_completion.description: GeoGebra application is open and active.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The GeoGebra interface (Algebra view, Graphics view, and toolbar) is visible in the screenshot.

task_completion.description: A horizon line is established at y=4.
task_completion.visual_evidence: A horizontal line is visible passing through the y=4 coordinate on the GeoGebra grid/axis.

task_completion.description: Two vanishing points are placed on the horizon line.
task_completion.visual_evidence: Two distinct points are visible on the line at y=4, with construction lines converging toward them.

task_completion.description: A grid is constructed using lines converging to the vanishing points.
task_completion.visual_evidence: A set of lines (at least 5 in each direction) converging to the two vanishing points, forming a 2-point perspective layout.

task_completion.description: The grid features mathematically accurate depth spacing (e.g., via diagonal method).
task_completion.visual_evidence: Presence of construction lines (like diagonals) that intersect the grid corners, proving depth was calculated rather than estimated by eye.

task_completion.description: The file is saved with the specific name in the correct directory.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The GeoGebra title bar or a 'Save As' dialog shows the filename 'perspective_grid.ggb'.

integrity.description: The agent used the GeoGebra GUI to perform the construction.
integrity.visual_evidence: Screenshots show the mouse cursor interacting with GeoGebra tools (Point, Line, Intersect) rather than just a final image appearing.

integrity.description: The agent did not simply import an image of a grid.
integrity.visual_evidence: The Algebra view (left sidebar) shows a list of geometric objects (Point A, Line f, etc.) created during the process.

integrity.description: The agent used the file menu or shortcut to save the work.
integrity.visual_evidence: The file menu is seen open or a save confirmation dialog appears with the correct path/filename.

privileged_info_for_vlm: The horizon line must be exactly at y=4. A 4x4 checkerboard requires a minimum of 10 grid lines (5 in each direction). To be mathematically accurate, the agent must use construction techniques like the Diagonal Method (lines passing through opposite corners of squares must meet at a vanishing point on the horizon) or Measuring Points. The final file must be named 'perspective_grid.ggb'.
